trickyParts: The relaunch does real filesystem work, so the fixture must await the relaunch's own worker-started publish (a resolver inside the fake publishRole) rather than a setImmediate tick budget: the first full-suite run failed one LEGION-93 test because flushEventLoopUntil's 5000 ticks ran out before launchWorker wrote the fresh claim, so /worker/ready saw generation 1. Same pattern the ready-time relaunch tests at the bottom of the LEGION-60 block already use.

Verdict ordering: retireDeadClaim (the stop) runs before promptRetires/promptFailures are written and before removeFromQueue, so a StopFailed leaves locator, counters, and queue entry untouched; the close handler's markWorkerDead then finds the locator already cleared (no second retirement) and its promoteWorkerQueue finds no queue entry (no relaunch).
Log wording follows the spec amendment (`3 prompts with no turn started`, `(bound 2)`), not the plan's literal strings, because promptFailures also counts refused prompts (LEGION-60).

The CI test job runs the real e2e suites under LEGION_E2E=1 (10 skips locally); real-prompt-delivery-e2e.test.ts asserts the prompt-failure accounting on a real tmux pane + worker-shim and had to follow the new zero-at-retire rule. It is deliberately not run on this box (scratch tmux server), so its proof is the pull request's CI run.
